title: Take Inventory apply: the stale-count check races a concurrent write it never locks against

context.prTitle: Add Take Inventory page for physical stock counting
context.prSummary: Adds a routed Take Inventory page (/take-inventory, TakeInventoryComponent) where an operator counts physical storage stock per product. Confirming an unchanged count is frontend-only; a non-zero difference reuses the existing positive Restock movement (increase) or Correction movement (decrease) through a new Inventory.Application.InventoryCounting.ApplyInventoryCount use case behind IInventoryCountAdjustmentStore (implemented by EfInventoryCountAdjustmentStore), never MachineRefill. The use case re-reads the authoritative current quantity (GetCurrentStockAsync) at the mutation boundary and throws DomainConflictException (409) when it no longer matches the quantity the operator counted against (ExpectedCurrentStock), refusing a stale count instead of silently overwriting a concurrent change. A positive difference uses the same restock-cost suggestion (last purchase cost, else average unit cost) an operator-entered manual Restock already offers, refusing Apply with a validation error when neither is available. Adds InventoryCountController, the frontend routing/component and docs/architecture.md Take Inventory section.
context.linkedIssue: #245 "Take Inventory page for physical stock counting" (risk Medium: new stock-mutating endpoint reusing existing Restock/Correction movement and costing rules)
acceptanceCriteria: Given an operator counts a product's physical storage stock and the counted value equals the authoritative current stock, when Apply runs, then no StockAdjustment is written and the outcome is Confirmed.

Given a counted value above the current stock, when Apply runs, then the positive difference is recorded as the existing positive Restock movement (never MachineRefill), using the same restock-cost suggestion (last purchase cost, else average unit cost) an operator-entered manual Restock already offers, and Apply is refused with a validation error when neither cost is available.
Given a counted value below the current stock, when Apply runs, then the negative difference is recorded as the existing Correction movement.

Given the authoritative current stock has changed since the operator started the count (the request's ExpectedCurrentStock no longer matches it), when Apply runs, then it refuses with a 409 and records nothing, instead of silently overwriting a concurrent change with a count based on stale UI state.

Both non-zero outcomes persist an ordinary StockAdjustment through the same costing/rebuild transaction every other stock movement in this document uses, so a count difference is auditable in Stock History exactly like a manual Restock or Correction.
docs/architecture.md documents Take Inventory: the three count outcomes, the reused Restock/Correction movement semantics, and the stale-count refusal.
outOfScope: A durable count-session/history record of confirmed-unchanged rows; the green/confirmed row state is frontend/session state only, and a durable record would be its own schema change and issue.
Any change to MachineRefill, Sync Restock, or the pick-list refill flow.
Any change to the existing manual Restock/Correction movement rules or their restock-cost suggestion themselves.
context.documentationImpact: Decision: UPDATED. Evidence: docs/architecture.md gains a "Take Inventory (issue #245)" section describing the three count-adjustment outcomes, the reused Restock/Correction movement semantics, the stale-count 409 refusal, and the controller/use-case/adapter shape.

Treat it as the exact-SHA validation evidence for this review.

findings.summary: ApplyInventoryCount.Handle reads the authoritative current quantity (GetCurrentStockAsync) with no transaction or lock around it, and EfInventoryCountAdjustmentStore.ApplyAsync only opens its own, later transaction at the write. A count or another stock write that commits in the gap between the read and that write is invisible to the staleness check, so a stale count can still be applied to a quantity nobody counted even though the 409 refusal claims to prevent exactly that, and no test exercises two overlapping requests - only a single mocked read followed by a single write.

source: Introducing PR identified from git history: commit 6b5ade799d290fb2c4e59710cbf047c43a305df0 "Add Take Inventory page for physical stock counting" (closes #245), merged to develop in PR #267 (merge commit 759d2fa7eca5dc97b42c77e61fbe4362c9966845; base 6e529ecb2386c8ad653d3dcbbf7fcbb063a68705 is the merge-base; head f49fcc313ab6295c29d9d426445e1dbbd54fd997 is a trivial merge-from-develop touching only docs/architecture.md, tree-identical to develop immediately after 759d2fa7). `git log --follow` on backend/Inventory.Application/InventoryCounting/ApplyInventoryCount.cs shows exactly two commits ever touched it: 6b5ade79 (creation, this case's head) and the fix below; `git show f49fcc31:.../EfInventoryCountAdjustmentStore.cs` confirms GetCurrentStockAsync is an AsNoTracking read with no surrounding transaction and ApplyAsync opens a separate, later transaction, unchanged until the fix. This is also the PR evals/agent/README.md Review-judgment scenarios (issue #268) names as the original incident behind INV-005/INV-006: a reviewer found the same read/write race against this PR's own concurrency acceptance criterion and called it non-blocking because the legacy flow was worse. Fixed by commit 0e6b8dacf61ef5bd8c78f9e9445546be9fb32b1e "Read stock inside the write lock for counts and adjustments (#1241)", merged to develop in PR #1270 (merge commit 06964a8f78f92c43956f9600c7048694105ade08): ApplyInventoryCount.Handle now opens IInventoryCountAdjustmentStore.BeginWriteTransactionAsync (SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE) before GetCurrentStockAsync and commits after ApplyAsync. The same fix PR separately locks EfStockAdjustmentStore's manual-adjustment staging (audit finding INV-04's other half, a different, unrelated code path with its own multi-step Clean Architecture migration history and no single clean introducing commit); that half is not covered by this case. Audit #1230 finding INV-04.
